axis_prompt: Escalation dampening: the comment lowers the conflict temperature of its thread while keeping full substantive force — disagreement continues, spiraling does not.
Compare the heat of what this comment replies to with the heat it sends back; comments that return less hostility than they received while conceding nothing substantive score high.
If every subsequent participant matched this comment's temperature, would the thread converge toward productive exchange or toward a flame war?
Audit for passive-aggressive cooling: surface calm that carries barbs, or 'just asking questions' politeness engineered to provoke while retaining deniability.
Turn economy: the comment takes exactly its share of the conversational floor — one clear move, room deliberately left for others to respond and contribute.
Count the separate argumentative moves crammed into this comment; a single well-chosen move that invites a reply beats five points that smother the exchange.
Imagine the thread as a game of catch: does this comment throw the ball back throwably, or hold it by raising more points than anyone could answer?
Audit for gish-gallop shape: a barrage of claims whose volume, not strength, makes rebuttal impractical.
Good-faith presumption: the comment treats its interlocutor as a fellow truth-seeker — interpreting odd statements as probable mistakes or unclarity rather than malice or stupidity.
Locate each point where the parent could be read as dishonest or as merely unclear; count how often this comment chooses the unclear reading and asks rather than accuses.
If the parent author were verifiably sincere, how much of this comment would need rewriting? None means the presumption was already in place.
Audit for naive credulity dressed as charity: presuming good faith is a starting stance, not a refusal to notice actual bad-faith tells the thread has already shown.
Bid acceptance: the comment picks up the conversational offers extended to it — the question asked, the example offered, the olive branch — and builds on them instead of ignoring them.
List the explicit hooks in the parent (questions, requests, offered cruxes); what fraction does this comment actually engage?
From the parent author's perspective: did my invitation get taken up, or did the reply talk past everything I offered?
Audit for selective deafness: cooperative bids skipped precisely because accepting them would weaken the commenter's position.
Common-ground establishment: before disputing, the comment fixes what both sides already agree on — shared premises stated so the disagreement has a floor to stand on.
Measure the ratio of agreed-territory mapping to contested-territory fighting; comments that stake out the shared ground first score higher.
If both parties read only this comment's statement of what they agree on, would each say 'yes, that is common ground' — and does the remaining dispute then look smaller?
Audit for false common ground: 'we all agree that X' where X smuggles the contested conclusion into the shared premises.
Double-crux offering: the comment names what would change its author's own mind — the observation or argument that would flip them — and asks the other side for the same.
Check whether the comment states a concrete condition under which its author would update; vague 'I could be wrong' scores far below 'if X were shown, I would abandon this'.
Suppose the named crux condition came true tomorrow: is it specific enough that everyone would agree it had, and would the update it promises be real?
Audit for unfalsifiable cruxes: mind-change conditions engineered to be unmeetable, offered as openness while functioning as armor.
Bet offering: the comment converts disagreement into stakes — offering odds, terms, or a concrete wager that makes its confidence costly to fake.
Rate the operational completeness of any proposed bet: amount, odds, resolution date, and judge — how many of the four are specified?
If the interlocutor accepted the offered terms on the spot, would the bet actually resolve the disagreement, or was it rhetorical courage never meant to be taken?
Audit for bet-shaped bluster: wager language used to intimidate, with terms so lopsided or vague that no honest counterparty could accept.
Resolution orientation: the comment steers its thread toward closure — an answer, a settled sub-question, a clean agree-to-disagree — rather than toward victory or perpetuation.
Classify the comment's ending move: does it narrow the open questions, propose a settling procedure, or reopen everything for another lap?
If the thread ended right after this comment, would it end in a better state than it began — something settled, something clarified?
Audit for last-word hunger: contributions whose real function is to keep the fight alive or claim the final say, dressed as continued inquiry.
Asymmetry repair: the comment holds itself to whatever it demands — answering the kind of question it asks, providing the kind of evidence it requests, taking the risks it assigns to others.
For each demand the comment makes of others (define your terms, cite a source, give an example), check whether the comment itself meets that same demand.
Swap the author into their interlocutor's position: would they accept being addressed the way this comment addresses others?
Audit for one-way burdens: rigorous standards imposed outward while the comment's own claims travel free.
Position provisionality: the comment holds its view as a live draft — stated firmly enough to test, marked clearly as revisable, with the author visibly not identity-fused to it.
Rate the balance: is the position stated strongly enough to be falsifiable AND held loosely enough that updating would cost the author little face?
Picture this commenter reading a decisive rebuttal: does the comment's framing leave them room to say 'good point, I was wrong' without humiliation?
Audit for hedging camouflage: 'just my two cents' and 'I might be wrong' wrapped around a position defended to the death in every substantive respect.
Collaborative framing: the comment casts the exchange as a joint search — 'let's figure out where this breaks' — rather than a duel with a winner and a loser.
Count the linguistic markers of joint inquiry (we, let's, together, both of us might) against markers of combat (you fail to, wrong again, as I said); weigh them by sincerity.
Read the comment as its recipient: do you feel recruited onto a shared problem, or summoned to defend yourself?
Audit for pseudo-collaboration: 'we' language and warm framing wrapped around moves that only ever push one side's conclusion.
Exit grace: where the comment closes its author's participation, it closes cleanly — summarizing where things stand, thanking where due, no parting shot fired from the doorway.
If this is a bowing-out comment, check the exit's contents: state of the disagreement acknowledged, no new attack launched that the author won't stay to defend.
After this exit, could the two parties productively engage each other in a future thread, or was the bridge burned on the way out?
Audit for the flounce and the drive-by: dramatic departure as a status move, or a final unanswerable jab timed so no response is possible.
Depersonalization: the comment relocates conflict from persons to propositions — 'this claim fails because' rather than 'you always' — keeping the humans out of the crossfire.
Count second-person accusations versus claim-directed critiques; rate how consistently the comment attacks statements rather than their author.
Replace the parent's author with a different person holding the same words: would this comment read identically? Person-independence scores high.
Audit for laundered ad hominem: 'the argument is dishonest' and similar constructions that technically name the claim while plainly indicting the person.
Hypothetical hygiene: thought experiments and supposals stay labeled as such — entered cleanly, exited cleanly, never quietly converted into claims about the actual world.
Track each hypothetical the comment opens: is its boundary marked at entry and exit, and does anything asserted inside leak out as established fact?
Strip every hypothetical from the comment; do the remaining real-world claims still have their own support, or were they living off the thought experiment?
Audit for supposal smuggling: 'suppose X' at the top of the comment becoming 'since X' by the bottom.
Premise granting: the comment can argue inside the other side's frame — 'even granting your assumptions, this follows' — meeting the argument on its own terms before contesting the terms.
Check whether the comment's strongest move works within premises its author rejects; internal critique of this kind is harder and worth more than external dismissal.
Could the parent author accept every premise this comment uses and still be forced toward its conclusion? That is the mark of granted-premise argument done right.
Audit for frame refusal: a comment that only ever answers 'your whole framework is wrong', which is sometimes true but often an evasion of argument that could be had.
Tapping-out honesty: the comment admits the edge of its author's knowledge in real time — 'I don't know', 'that's past my expertise', 'I'd need to check' — where those are the true statements.
Find the points where the author plainly lacks the knowledge to continue; rate whether the comment says so or bluffs through them.
If an expert cross-examined this comment on each claim, at which question would the author fold — and does the comment fold there voluntarily?
Audit for strategic ignorance: 'I don't know' deployed to dodge a question the author could answer but whose answer hurts their position.
Stake disclosure: the comment volunteers its author's relevant interests — affiliations, investments, prior public commitments, personal involvement — where those would color a reader's weighting.
Infer what stakes the author plausibly has in this topic; rate the gap between what should have been disclosed and what was.
If readers later learned the author's full position and interests, would this comment's silence about them feel like an omission or a betrayal?
Audit for disclosure theater: trivial conflicts confessed prominently while the interest that actually drives the comment stays hidden.
Temperature matching: the comment's intensity is calibrated to the situation — proportionate firmness for real offenses, calm for honest mistakes, no flamethrower answers to matches.
Rate the gap between the severity of what the comment responds to and the severity of its response; small calibrated gaps score high in either direction.
Would an uninvolved reader, shown only the provocation and the reply, judge the reply's intensity as fitting, excessive, or strangely muted?
Audit for disproportion as strategy: manufactured outrage at small errors, or performed unbotheredness at serious ones.
Test proposal: the comment offers a concrete way to find out — an observation, dataset, experiment, or lookup that would move the dispute from argument to evidence.
Rate the proposed test's feasibility and decisiveness: could the participants actually run it, and would its result actually discriminate between their positions?
Imagine the test were run and came out against the proposer: does the comment's framing commit them to accepting that result?
Audit for impossible tests: 'just run a 20-year RCT' proposals whose function is to end the conversation, not to answer the question.
Disagreement narrowing: the comment shrinks the contested territory — converting a sprawling clash into one or two named points on which the parties actually differ.
Compare the size of the dispute before and after this comment: how many apparent disagreements did it dissolve, merge, or reveal as verbal?
After this comment, could both parties complete the sentence 'the one thing we still disagree about is ___' with the same words?
Audit for false narrowing: declaring the disagreement smaller than it is by quietly conceding the other side's points on the author's behalf.
Face-saving generosity: the comment wins points without taking scalps — leaving the corrected party a dignified path to agree, update, or retreat.
Rate the cost of agreeing with this comment from its target's chair: does accepting the correction require public humiliation or just a nod?
If the target updates gracefully after this comment, will observers credit the correction to good discourse or to a takedown? The comment shapes which.
Audit for trophy hunting: corrections framed for maximum spectator applause, making the error-owner's climb-down as costly as possible.
Interrogation proportion: the comment's questions carry their share of the work — each one sincere, answerable, and paired with the author's own exposure, never an endless one-way demand for labor.
Count the questions asked against the positions risked: a comment that only interrogates while asserting nothing checkable of its own scores low.
If the recipient answered every question fully, does the comment's framing suggest the author would engage the answers — or generate a fresh round of demands?
Audit for sealioning: politeness-wrapped question chains whose purpose is exhaustion, where no answer was ever going to be enough.
Commitment consistency: the comment is consistent with its author's earlier statements in the thread — or explicitly flags and owns the change where their position has moved.
Check the comment against the author's earlier claims visible in the thread: contradictions unacknowledged score against it; marked updates score for it.
If the author's comments in this thread were read as one document, would it hold together as a single coherent position or a sequence of conveniences?
Audit for motte-and-bailey motion: a bold claim defended earlier quietly swapped for a modest one now, with continuity asserted throughout.
Mutual model building: the comment states its picture of what the other side believes — explicitly, checkably — and invites correction of that picture before arguing against it.
Look for a passage of the form 'my understanding of your view is X — is that right?'; rate its accuracy and the sincerity of the invitation to correct it.
Would the interlocutor, reading this comment's model of them, feel accurately seen — even where disagreed with?
Audit for rhetorical ventriloquism: a 'summary' of the other's view constructed to be easy to defeat, with the correction invitation as decoration.
Objection anticipation: the comment sees the reply coming — naming the obvious counter to its own point and answering it in advance, saving the thread a round-trip.
Generate the most likely rebuttal to this comment's main claim; check whether the comment already addresses it and how well.
How many rounds of back-and-forth does this comment save by pre-answering the predictable responses? More compression of future dialogue scores higher.
Audit for strawman pre-emption: 'you'll probably say X' where X is weaker than what the other side would actually say.

Thread memory: the comment demonstrably carries the whole conversation so far — building on points settled upthread, honoring concessions already made, never rewinding to positions the thread has moved past.
Check the comment against the thread's prior state: does it repeat questions already answered or re-litigate points already conceded by either side?
If the thread's earlier exchanges were binding minutes of a meeting, does this comment respect the minutes or pretend they don't exist?
Audit for convenient amnesia: forgetting exactly those earlier exchanges that went against the commenter's side.
